exception.reason: UCR offers related study in myth, philosophy, art and heritage, including some work on ritual, religious freedom and the role of belief in cultural life. These courses support individual interests. The available UCR curriculum does not sustain a 24-course programme centred on religious traditions, interpretation of sacred texts and the study of lived religion.
exception.curriculumContext: The 180 EC part-time Religion and Worldviews route includes 30 EC of approved electives and a required 6 EC thesis following thesis preparation.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: The current workbook supports comparison in myth and ritual, world philosophy, religious imagery and civic life, freedom of religion, Buddhist accounts of self, and some spiritual life writing. We tested a feasible 24-course plan adding Western Art History, Life & Travel Writing and Native American Histories. These improve cultural and interpretive breadth. They do not supply a sequence in religious traditions, comparative interpretation of sacred texts or empirical research in religious communities. Generic methods, complementary perspectives, flexible topic choices and optional research were considered within their actual scope.

candidateAssessment.concept: Comparative religious cultures, texts and worldviews
candidateAssessment.assessment: The strongest feasible interdisciplinary plan includes direct work on myth and partial work on philosophy, belief, religious material culture and spiritual self-representation. Its complementary research and interpretive methods do not supply sustained work across religious traditions, sacred texts or lived practice.

Actual conflict, radicalisation and environmental courses can supply complementary perspectives; no required religion-centred inquiry or documented religious-environment/dialogue sequence is established. Rejection as merely redundant with the withdrawn public-life strand is superseded.

The specific art/literary/philosophical contributions do not establish theological/biblical interpretation, doctrine or lived-faith formation. Missing professional credentials are not used to reject the general comparative route.

Islamic courts as artistic context and comparative public law do not establish Islamic belief, history, exegesis or jurisprudence. Arabic remains support-only under the retained corrected evidence classification.

audience.programmeDescription: Theology and Religious Studies at VU Amsterdam examines religious traditions, beliefs, texts and practices and their place in society. The part-time Religion and Worldviews route combines comparative study of religions with philosophy, social science and research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers related courses in myth, philosophy, art and heritage. VU brings these perspectives together through sustained study of religious traditions, interpretation of sacred texts and research on lived religion. The curriculum below shows how that study develops at VU.

curriculum.limitation: The recommended part-time schedule covers 180 EC over six calendar years. Teaching is mainly in Dutch in the first two academic stages and in English in the third stage of this route.

componentNotes.stage3-minor: 30 EC of approved study. Options include a minor, academic electives or a placement of up to 12 EC with 18 EC of coursework.
componentNotes.stage3-01: Entry requires 120 EC in the programme and completion of all first-year and first-semester second-year courses.
componentNotes.stage3-05: The required 6 EC thesis follows successful completion of the thesis preparation lab.
